items.title: 21.7 Cosmic Redshift: Evidence for an Expanding Universe

source_refs.note: Topic 21.7 (PDF 175-176). Equation 21.4 printed with '>>' is corrected in a warning. The redshift example and check question are added; answers need review.

blocks.text: Cosmic redshift is the effect in which light from distant galaxies is stretched towards the red end of the spectrum. It happens because the universe is expanding, so galaxies are moving away from us and the wavelength of the light they emit increases. The greater the distance of a galaxy, the larger its redshift, that is, the faster it is moving away. By studying cosmic redshift, scientists can measure how fast the universe is expanding.

The observed change in wavelength is related to the relative velocity v between the source and the observer: z = dlambda/lambda = df/f = v/c (21.4), which holds approximately when v is much less than c. A positive dlambda indicates a redshift, showing that the object is moving away from Earth; a negative dlambda is a blueshift, showing that it is approaching. The light from faraway galaxies appears redder than expected because space itself is stretching as the universe expands, which also stretches the light waves. The redshift pattern is observed in all directions, which shows that the universe is expanding: it is not just that galaxies are moving apart through space, but that the space between them is increasing. These findings strongly support the Big Bang theory, which says the universe began in an extremely hot and dense state and has been growing ever since.

blocks.title: Equation 21.4
blocks.text: The book prints equation 21.4 as 'Z = dl/l >> df/f >> v/c'. The quantities are approximately equal, not much greater than one another: z = dlambda/lambda = df/f = v/c (the frequency shift has the opposite sign), valid for speeds much less than the speed of light.

A hydrogen line with a laboratory wavelength of 656.3 nm is observed at 662.9 nm in the spectrum of a galaxy. Find the galaxy's recession velocity. Solution: z = dlambda/lambda = (662.9 - 656.3)/656.3 = 0.0101, so v = zc = 0.0101 x 3.0 x 10^8 m s^-1 = 3.0 x 10^6 m s^-1, moving away.

blocks.prompt: A spectral line from a star is observed at a shorter wavelength than in the laboratory. What does this tell us?
blocks.explanation: It is a blueshift: the star is moving towards us.

items: Redshift: z = dlambda/lambda = v/c (for v much less than c); positive: moving away.
Redshift in all directions: space is expanding; supports the Big Bang.
